title: It Looks Painted, But Not a Drop Is Paint | China Travel Expert
description:
It looks hand-painted — but there isn't a single brushstroke of paint on it. Every color you see is crushed glass, fused in fire.

This is cloisonné — 景泰蓝, "Jingtai Blue." Artisans shape a bare copper body, bend flat copper wire by hand into thousands of tiny cells, pack each cell with colored enamel paste, then fire it in a kiln until the glass melts into color — over and over, then polished smooth. The craft took its name from the Ming dynasty's Jingtai reign (1449–1457) and blue was its signature ground; today it's one of China's national intangible cultural heritage metal crafts, with more than 600 years behind it.

🧭 Expert Tip: Buy from a working workshop kiln (Beijing has several you can tour) rather than a tourist-stall "antique" — you'll see the wires and firing marks that prove it's real cloisonné.
